text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call SREs — elevated p99 tail latency and streaming stalls detected across cross-zone paths for streaming-prod (eu-west2 / us-east-1). Automated alerts: p99 > 1200ms, streaming stalls rate +48% in last 5m. Investigate.

alex: acked. I'm on it. quick ask — is this global or localized to a few AZs?

incident-bot: Alerts show spike concentrated on azb/azc in eu-west2 and a subset of us-east-1 hosts. Error profiles: increased TLS handshake timeouts and DNS lookup retries.

jia: looking at `streaming-gateway` logs now. I see a lot of `TLS handshake timeout` and `write tcp: connection reset by peer` around 3732109800..3732109850. Posting sample:```
2026-03-15T12:34:21Z gateway-azb: tls: handshake timeout after 30s
2026-03-15T12:34:23Z gateway-azb: connection reset by peer
```

katy: could be NAT ephemeral exhaustion or routing asymmetry. Any signs of 5xx from upstream or packetloss counters?

mike: checking VPC flow logs and NAT metrics. `nat-azb-1` shows SNAT port usage at 92% and retransmits rising. TCP retransmit ratio jumped from 0.3% -> 3.8% in last 10m.

leo: DNS errors correlate — our local resolver in azc shows `SERVFAIL` spikes. I suspect packet loss to DNS resolvers or ECMP flapping.

alex: ok mitigation plan proposals: 1) throttle new streaming sessions for non-critical customers for 10m; 2) reroute egress from azb/azc to alternative NATs in same region; 3) enable short-term tcp keepalive tweak? Which is fastest?

jia: fastest is to add temporary SNAT capacity — spin up additional NAT gateway endpoints and update route-targets for streaming-gateway ASGs. I can push a traffic-steer to nat-azd-2.

ops-bot: Runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/network/nat-ephemeral-ports|NAT ephemeral ports runbook> — recommended steps for emergency add.

katy: while adding NATs, also start a canary shift: move 10% of streaming traffic in eu-west2 to dedicated pool `streaming-dedicated-2` (lower latency profile) and monitor p95/p99. Use canary policy `canary-traffic 10%` in console.

mike: executing: `aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-azd --allocation-id eipalloc-xxxx` then update route table `rtb-STREAM-OUT` to prefer nat-azd-2 via weight.

alex: I'll throttle non-prod keys via `rate_limit --tag nonprod --limit 50rps` to reduce burst pressure. Sara, can you assemble a quick customer impact note?

sara: on it. Current telemetry: 6% of streaming sessions experienced stalls >5s in last 10m, 0.8% total requests got TLS timeouts, top affected customers: a streaming partner (ID: cust-42) and a batch of heavy embedded apps. Draft: "We observed increased latency and streaming interruptions in eu-west2 and parts of us-east-1 affecting a small subset of customers; mitigation steps are underway." Will post in #customer-notifications after you review.

leo: I'm running packet captures on the egress path to the resolver; see a lot of dropped DNS responses and ~30% increased retransmit at the ToR -> NAT boundary.

jia: new NAT up and route updated. Traffic steering started at 3732109888, moving ~22% of traffic to nat-azd-2.

incident-bot: Automation observation: p99 dropped from 1250ms -> 680ms within 90s of route switch. Streaming stalls rate down from +48% -> +12% after reroute.

alex: good improvement. Keep observing. Next steps: 1) keep additional NATs up for 2 hours, 2) run DNS resolver failover tests, 3) add temporary ECMP pin for streaming to avoid path hopping, 4) if p99 persists escalate to network infra.

katy: I'm going to open a P1 ticket with network infra and tag them: @network-infra. Include packet captures and NAT port stats.

mike: adding DNS fallback to our internal resolvers: `resolvconf` change applied to gateway ASG — primary resolver moved to internal sentinel 10.2.1.12, secondary 10.2.1.13.

sara: customer note posted to #customer-notifications and sent to affected account managers. Link: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/3732109876/notice|incident notice>.

leo: packet captures and metrics uploaded to the incident doc. Observed pattern: egress queueing during bursts -> packet drops -> TLS handshake retransmits -> increased p99 tail. Suspect cross-AZ path asymmetry during peak egress.

jia: also noticed stream-router kernel drop counters increase right before stalls. Might be kernel-level conntrack backpressure on NAT instances. Will increase `conntrack_max` on the gateways and restart the small proxy process to free sockets. Command:```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
systemctl restart streaming-proxy
```

alex: apply conntrack bump now if safe — coordination with infra?

katy: do it, but roll sequentially in azb then azc, watch connection drops. Jia proceed.

jia: applied conntrack bump in azb at 3732109920 and restarted proxy. Monitoring.

incident-bot: Observability: after conntrack bump + NAT reroute + DNS fallback, p99 steady ~420ms, stalls <3%. No increase in application errors.

mike: good. I'm leaving the extra NAT up for 2 hours and will schedule a cleanup task to revert route preferences to standard weighting after 2h if stable.

katy: handoff: I'm assigning next oncall jia for followups and to coordinate post-incident RCA. @jia you'll be the on-call owner for the next 4 hours — escalate to me for any regressions.

jia: ack, I'll own RCA and coordinate with network infra for deeper path analysis (ECMP behavior and ToR health).

alex: thanks team. Post-incident items: 1) automate NAT scaling when SNAT > 80% for streaming customers, 2) add guardrail to failover DNS resolvers for streaming-gateway, 3) add conntrack visibility to runtime dashboards, 4) update runbook with ECMP pinning and route weight play.

sara: drafting internal incident summary and customer follow-up. Will attach timeline and mitigations.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in place, severity reduced to S2, monitoring. Incident channel will remain open for RCA notes. :white_check_mark:
